Energy | Congressman Mike Kennedy Skip to main content Energy As your Congressman, I understand that affordable and reliable energy is essential to the health, security, and economic well-being of our communities. I support an all-of-the-above energy approach that embraces American oil, natural gas, nuclear, geothermal, and all other energy production. I also recognize that energy independence is critical to keeping costs low for families and businesses. Too often, excessive federal red tape and bureaucratic delays stifle innovation, restrict access to our resources, and undermine the states that are responsibly leading the way in domestic energy production. I strongly support Utah’s efforts to expand energy development and believe states, not Washington bureaucrats, are best positioned to manage their resources safely and effectively. I am committed to cutting unnecessary regulations, streamlining permitting, and advancing policies that strengthen domestic production, protect jobs, and ensure America remains energy secure. Kennedy Introduces Bipartisan Bill to Reduce Medical Billing Burden on Native American Patients May 7, 2026 Press Release Washington, D.C. — Congressman Mike Kennedy, M.D. (UT-03) introduced H.R. 8658,  the Indian Health Service Emergency Claims Parity Act to give American Indian and Alaska Native patients a fair window to handle paperwork after a medical emergency. The bill extends the Purchased/Referred Care (PRC) notification deadline from 72 hours to 15 days. It is a commonsense fix that prevents patients from being saddled with bills simply because they were focused on getting well. Economy | Congressman Mike Kennedy Skip to main content Economy Utah has one of the strongest economies in the nation. Our state leads on job creation, entrepreneurship, and economic freedom because Utahns are hardworking, innovative, and trusted to make their own decisions. The best thing the federal government can do for our economy is get out of the way. For too long, Washington has grown bigger while American paychecks have grown smaller. Burdensome regulations, runaway spending, and a tax code that punishes work and investment have made it harder for families to get ahead and for small businesses to compete. I believe the answer isn't more federal programs or another agency in D.C., it's pushing power, dollars, and decisions back to the states, communities, and families who actually live with the consequences. I'm committed to cutting red tape that strangles small businesses, reining in regulatory agencies that have stretched far beyond their intended purpose, and empowering Utah. A smaller Washington means a stronger Utah. When we trust families to spend their own money, trust businesses to compete on a level playing field, and trust states to govern themselves our economy can thrive. My belief is that when Utah leads, America wins. For more information concerning work and views related to Economy, please  contact our office. Healthcare | Congressman Mike Kennedy Skip to main content Healthcare After more than 25 years as a family practice physician, I've seen our healthcare system from the inside, and I know it's broken. Costs are too high, care is too tangled in red tape, and too many hardworking families are paying more for insurance they can barely afford to use. Making healthcare affordable again is one of my top priorities in Congress. Since Obamacare passed, deductibles and out-of-pocket costs have skyrocketed, leaving millions of Americans with coverage on paper they can't actually use. I'm leading legislation to put patients back in charge through price transparency and expanded health savings accounts, and to stop the insurance-driven prior authorization requests and mandated step therapies that delay critical care. On prescription drugs, I support the Trump Administration's efforts to negotiate lower prices, and I've backed legislation to ensure drug rebates go directly to patients rather than getting absorbed by PBMs. And to address the shortage of healthcare workers, particularly in rural Utah, I've introduced legislation to streamline apprenticeship pathways for aspiring nurses and medical assistants. You deserve a healthcare system built around your health, your wallet, and your choices, not the bureaucracies and middlemen standing between you and your doctor. For more information concerning Rep. Environment | Congressman Mike Kennedy Skip to main content Environment I believe responsible stewardship of our land means protecting both the people who call it home and the landscapes that define our state. Utah's forests, rangelands, and public lands face dangers and issues that distant federal offices rarely grasp, and years of mismanagement and inaction have left too many acres overgrown, mismanaged, and vulnerable to catastrophic wildfire and more. I support proactive forest management and closer coordination with our state and local partners to reduce wildfire risk and protect communities, watersheds, and wildlife habitat. These tools are proven, science-based, and far preferable to watching millions of our acres burn each summer. Utah's public lands should remain open and accessible for recreation, hunting, grazing, and responsible use, not locked away and mismanaged by distant bureaucrats. By empowering states, standing with our foresters, and prioritizing active management, we can preserve Utah's landscape and pass it on safer, healthier, and more resilient than we found it. Border Security | Congressman Mike Kennedy Skip to main content Border Security Border security is national security. The federal government has a clear duty to enforce our laws, secure our borders, and stop the flow of fentanyl, human trafficking, and criminal activity that has devastated communities from Utah to the southern border. At the same time, our legal immigration system is broken, outdated, inefficient, and failing both American workers and those trying to come here the right way. I support securing the border, ending catch and release, and giving the men and women of law enforcement the tools and backing they need to do their jobs. We also need to modernize legal immigration so it's orderly, lawful, and aligned with the needs of our economy, all while upholding the rule of law that makes this country worth coming to in the first place. The American people deserve an immigration system that is secure, fair, and puts the safety of our communities first.
